anomalies.observed: On the FCC sheet, NET0021 is connected to FCC2.94 (BOOT0) and to the switch marked “Reset Switch” (SW5); FCC2.14 (NRST) has no shown connection. The switch marked “Bootmode Switch” (SW4) is driven through R65 from NET0176, which is connected to FCC2.20 (VREF+), rather than BOOT0.
anomalies.expected: The reset switch should act on NRST, and the boot-mode switch should select the BOOT0 level. VREF+ should not be used as the boot-mode control net.

evidence.quote: FCC2: pin 14 NRST; pin 94 BOOT0 is labelled NET0021; pin 20 VREF+ is labelled NET0176. SW5 is labelled “Reset Switch” and connects to NET0021; SW4 is labelled “Bootmode Switch” and connects through R65 to NET0176. (Flight Control Computer, page 2/6)
NAVC counterpart: NRST is NET0073 and connects to the “Reset Switch”; BOOT0 is NET0124 and connects to the “Bootmode Switch”. (Navigation Computer, page 3/6)

anomalies.impact: The FCC reset button does not reset the MCU, and the boot-mode selector does not control BOOT0; instead it changes the VREF+ network. This can prevent normal reset and make selecting the intended boot mode impossible, while also disturbing the MCU's analog reference.

parsed.summary: The FCC reset and boot-mode switch nets are misconnected: reset is routed to BOOT0, boot-mode selection is routed to VREF+, and NRST is left unconnected in the drawing. The NAVC sheet shows the intended separate NRST and BOOT0 switch connections.
